1472:     --------
1473:     dtw : Get the similarity score for DTW
1474:     subsequence_cost_matrix: Calculate the required cost matrix
1475:     subsequence_path: Calculate a matching path manually
1476:     """
1477:     be = instantiate_backend(be, subseq, longseq)
1478:     subseq = to_time_series(subseq, be=be)
1479:     longseq = to_time_series(longseq, be=be)
1480:     acc_cost_mat = subsequence_cost_matrix(subseq=subseq, longseq=longseq, be=be)
1481:     global_optimal_match = be.argmin(acc_cost_mat[-1, :])
1482:     path = subsequence_path(acc_cost_mat, global_optimal_match, be=be)
1483:     return path, be.sqrt(acc_cost_mat[-1, :][global_optimal_match])
1484: 
1485: 
1486: @njit()
1487: def njit_sakoe_chiba_mask(sz1, sz2, radius=1):
1488:     """Compute the Sakoe-Chiba mask.
1489: 
1490:     Parameters
1491:     ----------
1492:     sz1 : int
1493:         The size of the first time series
1494:     sz2 : int
1495:         The size of the second time series.
1496:     radius : int
1497:         The radius of the band.
1498: 
1499:     Returns
1500:     -------
1501:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
1502:         Sakoe-Chiba mask.
1503: 
1504:     Examples
1505:     --------
1506:     >>> njit_sakoe_chiba_mask(4, 4, 1)
1507:     array([[ True,  True, False, False],
1508:            [ True,  True,  True, False],
1509:            [False,  True,  True,  True],
1510:            [False, False,  True,  True]])
1511:     >>> njit_sakoe_chiba_mask(7, 3, 1)
1512:     array([[ True,  True, False],
1513:            [ True,  True,  True],
1514:            [ True,  True,  True],
1515:            [ True,  True,  True],
1516:            [ True,  True,  True],
1517:            [ True,  True,  True],
1518:            [False,  True,  True]])
1519:     """
1520:     mask = numpy.full((sz1, sz2), False)
1521:     if sz1 > sz2:
1522:         width = sz1 - sz2 + radius
1523:         for i in prange(sz2):
1524:             lower = max(0, i - radius)
1525:             upper = min(sz1, i + width) + 1
1526:             mask[lower:upper, i] = True
1527:     else:
1528:         width = sz2 - sz1 + radius
1529:         for i in prange(sz1):
1530:             lower = max(0, i - radius)
1531:             upper = min(sz2, i + width) + 1
1532:             mask[i, lower:upper] = True
1533:     return mask
1534: 
1535: 
1536: def sakoe_chiba_mask(sz1, sz2, radius=1, be=None):
1537:     """Compute the Sakoe-Chiba mask.
1538: 
1539:     Parameters
1540:     ----------
1541:     sz1 : int
1542:         The size of the first time series
1543:     sz2 : int
1544:         The size of the second time series.
1545:     radius : int
1546:         The radius of the band.
1547:     be : Backend object or string or None
1548:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
1549:         the NumPy backend is used.
1550:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
1551:         the PyTorch backend is used.
1552:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
1553:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
1554: 
1555:     Returns
1556:     -------
1557:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
1558:         Sakoe-Chiba mask.
1559: 
1560:     Examples
1561:     --------
1562:     >>> sakoe_chiba_mask(4, 4, 1)
1563:     array([[ True,  True, False, False],
1564:            [ True,  True,  True, False],
1565:            [False,  True,  True,  True],
1566:            [False, False,  True,  True]])
1567:     >>> sakoe_chiba_mask(7, 3, 1)
1568:     array([[ True,  True, False],
1569:            [ True,  True,  True],
1570:            [ True,  True,  True],
1571:            [ True,  True,  True],
1572:            [ True,  True,  True],
1573:            [ True,  True,  True],
1574:            [False,  True,  True]])
1575:     """
1576:     warnings.warn(
1577:         "This method is deprecated, use tslearn.metrics.sakoe_chiba_mask instead.",
1578:         DeprecationWarning
1579:     )
1580: 
1581:     be = instantiate_backend(be)
1582:     mask = be.full((sz1, sz2), False)
1583:     if sz1 > sz2:
1584:         width = sz1 - sz2 + radius
1585:         for i in range(sz2):
1586:             lower = max(0, i - radius)
1587:             upper = min(sz1, i + width) + 1
1588:             mask[lower:upper, i] = True
1589:     else:
1590:         width = sz2 - sz1 + radius
1591:         for i in range(sz1):
1592:             lower = max(0, i - radius)
1593:             upper = min(sz2, i + width) + 1
1594:             mask[i, lower:upper] = True
1595:     return mask
1596: 
1597: 
1598: @njit()
1599: def _njit_itakura_mask(sz1, sz2, max_slope=2.0):
1600:     """Compute the Itakura mask without checking that the constraints
1601:     are feasible. In most cases, you should use itakura_mask instead.
1602: 
1603:     Parameters
1604:     ----------
1605:     sz1 : int
1606:         The size of the first time series
1607: 
1608:     sz2 : int
1609:         The size of the second time series.
1610: 
1611:     max_slope : float (default = 2)
1612:         The maximum slope of the parallelogram.
1613: 
1614:     Returns
1615:     -------
1616:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
1617:         Itakura mask.
1618:     """
1619:     min_slope = 1 / float(max_slope)
1620:     max_slope *= float(sz1) / float(sz2)
1621:     min_slope *= float(sz1) / float(sz2)
1622: 
1623:     lower_bound = numpy.empty((2, sz2))
1624:     lower_bound[0] = min_slope * numpy.arange(sz2)
1625:     lower_bound[1] = (sz1 - 1) - max_slope * (sz2 - 1) + max_slope * numpy.arange(sz2)
1626:     lower_bound_ = numpy.empty(sz2)
1627:     for i in prange(sz2):
